sentences.text:
These two petitions are filed by husband and in-laws of respondent No.2, seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in Crime No.44/2024, for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 354,
354A, 354B, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 IPC.
2.
Today, a joint affidavit has been filed by the husband/petitioner in Crl.P.No.13132/2025 and the second respondent/wife.
In the joint affidavit, it is stated that the NC: 2025:KHC:38975 HC-KAR matter between the parties, in M.C. No.846/2024, has been amicably settled.
Pursuant to the settlement, the marriage between the petitioner/husband and the second respondent/wife has been dissolved, as reflected in the divorce decree dated 10.09.2025.

The second respondent/complainant,
who is present before this Court, admits that the marriage has been legally dissolved and, in view thereof, has requested that the proceedings pending in the above-mentioned crime number be quashed.
3. Although the matter has been amicably settled, the offences under Section 498A IPC are non- compoundable.

In light of the dissolution of marriage and in the interest of giving a quietus to the dispute, this Court finds it appropriate to exercise its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the criminal proceedings.

4. Accordingly, this Court passes the following:
NC: 2025:KHC:38975 HC-KAR ORDER (i) The petitions are allowed.

(ii) The proceedings pending in Crime No.44/2024, for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 354, 354A, 354B, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 IPC, before the Mr. Rahul Agrawal vs State Of Karnataka on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16270618/
